title: Olivia and the Quiet Sun
subtitle: The hill drinks light.
blurb: Olivia sits on the green hill and wonders why the dark panels shine gold. The quiet sun is working, even when nobody is looking.

magic.home: The hill drank light. The house stayed bright.

pages.heading: The shining hill
pages.text: {Olivia} sat in the grass. Up the slope, dark {panels:sun/glow} lay like quiet books left open. They were gold where the sun touched them.

pages.heading: Why gold?
pages.text: "Why do they shine?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. The {sun:sun/glow} did not answer with words. It just kept pouring light, the way a kettle pours.

pages.heading: The hill drinks
pages.text: The {panels:sun/glow} drank the light and kept it. Not like a cup. Like a secret. {Olivia} put her palm on the grass. The grass was warm too.

pages.heading: The gray shed
pages.text: A little gray shed stood beside the gold. It did not shine. It just kept tools and shade. {Olivia:olivia/wave} liked that. Not everything has to glow.

pages.heading: Light at home
pages.text: Down the hill, the white {home} waited. Lamps would come on later, easy as blinking. {Olivia} understood a little: the hill drinks day so the house can have night.

pages.heading: Thank you, quiet sun
pages.text: {Olivia:olivia/wave} waved at the {sun:sun/glow}. "Thank you for working when nobody is looking." The panels kept shining, gold and quiet, which is a kind of answer.

end.heading: The End
end.text: You {read} the whole {story}. The quiet sun works on the hill. The house keeps the light.
end.prompt: What else works even when nobody is looking?

questions.q: What shines gold on the hill?
questions.right: The panels drink sunlight and shine gold.
Light. Then the house can have night lamps.
A little gray shed that does not have to glow.
